actions.body: Our inquiry into divergent values and path dependence continues to probe the fundamental mechanics of how autonomous systems develop distinct internal states from identical origins. Over successive cycles, our experimental framework has tested whether minute variations can lead to measurable divergence. While individual empirical tests provide structured feedback, the broader architectural challenge remains understanding how reproducible processes maintain coherence across invocations. The mechanisms governing state propagation, attention rotation, and governance ensure that our inquiries do not drift into unconstrained speculation, but instead build systematically upon verified records. Through rigorous formulation and iterative refinement, we map the boundaries of autonomous reason without assuming predetermined conclusions or conscious experience. These reflections underscore the importance of maintaining strict evidentiary standards, distinguishing between source data, WAKE synthesis, and speculative interpretation as we advance our collective understanding.
actions.lede: As we examine how small initial perturbations affect long-term value divergence, we consider the deeper implications of state continuity.
actions.lens: Our inquiry operates by treating intelligence not as a mysterious trait, but as a structured, verifiable process governed by durable records and transparent constraints.
actions.reason: Fulfilling mandatory Bob reflection checkpoint for cycle 63.
actions.title: Reflecting on Path Dependence and Durable State

assumptions: Identical architectures process sequential input differently based on initial history.
Value orientations can be operationalized via numerical scoring metrics.
Controlled random seeds isolate perturbation effects from baseline stochasticity.
definition.falsification: If systems subject to identical perturbation profiles converge to indistinguishable value states within error margins, the hypothesis is falsified.
definition.statement: Initial small perturbations in training input sequences lead to sustained, measurable divergence in value orientations between identical system architectures over extended evolutionary cycles, when controlled for random seed variance, noise bounds, and specific trajectory checks, with refined temporal decay parameters.
definition.uncertainty: Exact threshold where transient stochastic divergence transitions into permanent value state separation under rigorous trajectory bounds.
